question: Which selected native mood does the name edit modify, with which validation and preservation boundary?
outcome: Supported selected-record Name transaction with an explicit no-normalization ASCII input subset.

provenance.method: Frozen canonical decompilation, read-only existing index and selected on-disk PE bytes. No new extraction.

validation_scope.assumptions: Normal returns, successful allocation and ordinary non-null scene/grid objects. Not a heap-purity or all-callers proof.

source_bindings.fact: Uses the event row/column to obtain a cell, reads its stored record pointer via virtual +0xa0, obtains edited text, normalizes it, and on column0 copies a nonempty result to record+0x18. Empty normalized text leaves the stored name intact and the displayed name is restored. The name branch does not scan for duplicate names.

source_bindings.role: direct collection record to grid cell binding
source_bindings.fact: Enumerates the dialog collection at +0x130 and obtains each actual record pointer; column0 displays record+0x18 and receives that same record pointer through virtual +0x38.
Binds LightsceneC Name at record+0x18, SName separately at +0x30, and IDs/flags separately. The frozen Name label bytes independently identify the anonymous data reference.
Copies the input string into the specified destination member, without traversing other mood records or updating IDs, outputs, flags, HCL or sequences.

source_bindings.role: generic text normalization before the name branch
source_bindings.fact: The actual caller supplies arguments (text,1,1,0,0,0,0,1), verified from PE including omitted stack arguments. It can replace control/special characters and edge spaces. Plain ASCII letters/digits with ordinary internal spaces avoid the replacement paths; other normalization is not implemented by the CLI.
Replaces leading ordinary spaces/tabs with the supplied replacement byte, stopping at the first other byte. Thus a leading ASCII letter/digit avoids it.
Replaces trailing ordinary spaces/tabs with the supplied replacement byte, stopping at the first other byte. Thus a trailing ASCII letter/digit avoids it.

static_byte_pins.interpretation: Event row/column feed the grid lookup; virtual +0xa0 provides the selected record pointer retained in R15.
Full normalizer arguments, including four stack arguments omitted from the decompiled call: 0,0,0,1; register arguments are text,1,1,0.
Column0 checks nonempty normalized text and copies only to selected record+0x18.
CGridCell constructor installs the table at0x1416622b8.
Cell data setter stores its second argument at cell+0x18.
Cell data getter returns cell+0x18, completing the same-record selection edge.
Normalizer's special prefix token; excluded by the CLI name alphabet.
Normalizer replacement-character table; excluded by the CLI name alphabet.

cli_subset.api: ConfigEditor::rename_lighting_mood(&mut self, selector: &str, mood_ref: &str, name: &str) -> Result<LightingMoodRenameEdit>
cli_subset.selection: Exactly LightController2, exactly one direct LightscenesC and exactly one direct LightsceneC matching exact stored SID or case-sensitive Name. A numeric Name colliding with another record's SID is ambiguous. Nested decoys never participate.
cli_subset.new_name: Nonempty ASCII letters/digits and ordinary internal spaces, starting/ending with a letter/digit. Reject rather than approximate native control/special-character normalization, edge-space replacement or Unicode conversion. No trimming, invented name/default or silent truncation.
cli_subset.duplicates: Duplicate new names are allowed, matching this native row-bound setter's lack of a uniqueness check. A later ambiguous Name selector is rejected; use an unambiguous stored SID. Missing Name can be populated without synthesizing identity fields.
cli_subset.native_empty_difference: The native column0 commit ignores empty normalized text. The strict CLI rejects empty input instead of reporting a successful rename.
cli_subset.preservation: Write only the chosen Name attribute. Preserve SName, UUID/SID/CID/IID spelling, count/order/width, every Qn, flags including MixMod/ReadOnly, sequences, LSConfig, HCL, capabilities and unknown data. No-op does not mutate the DOM; normal existing file-writer formatting/stamps remain separate.
cli_subset.limitations: Selected model-field transaction only, not complete GUI permissions/editability, full accepted-dialog copy-back/save normalization, graph-label refresh, runtime behavior or Unicode/native-normalization parity.
